A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and Appendix A.1–A.3 are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on JSRT and WHU Building, including benchmark results and spatial-correlation sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original segmentation results and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: ECCD names the existing ELBO-computable discrete distribution. The latent Gaussian noise model, KMS/Kronecker covariance, ELBO objective, alternating updates in Algorithm 1 and inference procedure are retained. Expanded definitions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate JSRT lung, heart and clavicle segmentation and WHU building segmentation under the same synthetic-noise scenarios. Temporal sequences and higher-dimensional applications discussed in v2 are prospective, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the same evaluated comparators: CE, CoT, TriNet, JoCoR, SP, T-Loss, SC and EM, alongside the clean-label reference. The updated T-Loss citation does not establish a different evaluated method.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, preprocessing, binary-task setup, noise parameter grids, Dice/IoU metrics, architecture, optimizer and tuning procedure match. Algorithm 1 retains fixed prior parameters; v2 clarifies inconsistent optimization prose without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same correlation-parameter sensitivity curves and posterior label-error visualizations. Their accompanying findings are unchanged, and the appendices add no new ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: The error bars in Figure 3 and shaded bands in Figure 4 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The result graphics and numerical findings match. For example, Figure 3 reports the same 97.7 lung Dice at (alpha, beta) = (0.3, 0.5) and 87.4 WHU IoU at (phi, zeta, lambda) = (0.1, 0, 0.3). Figure 4 also retains the same curves and qualitative results.

T1.justification: v2 adds a special-case argument connecting the ELBO to ordinary cross-entropy and corrects transition-matrix normalization to sum over output class k in Eqs. (5)–(6). The core KMS and ELBO derivations in Appendix A remain equivalent apart from notation and rearrangement.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims first use of KMS as a scalable tool for variational inference and foregrounds applications to temporal sequences. v1 already introduced a distribution class and claimed applicability beyond 2D segmentation, so this refines the contribution scope rather than replacing it. The empirical robustness claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Broader Impact Statement explicitly warns that effectiveness may decline when label noise lacks stationary, exponentially decaying correlations. This adds a specific applicability limitation. Existing interpretations of the experiments and limitations concerning posterior storage and small or elongated structures are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly identifies the existing W and V transition matrices as learnable, and Section 4.3 clarifies that the prior remains fixed during the stated updates. These are documentation refinements; the reported implementation settings, initialization values and code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds graphical-model, CRF, time-series and Toeplitz references, including Koller–Friedman, Sutton–McCallum, Brockwell–Davis and Grenander–Szegö, while removing Blei et al. and Jordan et al. It positions KMS as an underused computational tool for variational inference. The substantive noisy-segmentation related-work comparison remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The method exposition is extensively rewritten into separate Problem Formulation and Proposed ECCD Framework sections, with a staged explanation of MLE, noisy-label likelihood and the ELBO. The abstract, contribution narrative and conclusion are revised, ECCD terminology is introduced, experimental subsections are expanded, and a Broader Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The document receives a comprehensive layout change, including the title and author block, typography, text width, headers and equation presentation. All four retained figures are substantially enlarged and repositioned, improving visibility of dense plots. Their scientific content is unchanged, and no new result figures or tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through the separated problem formulation, explicit probability definitions, corrected transition-matrix normalization and larger figures. The new correlation-assumption caveat also clarifies applicability. These gains are limited: empirical evidence and core appendix derivations remain unchanged, and temporal applications remain prospective. Minor editorial regressions, including Appendix A.2 retaining an outdated Eq. (3) reference, do not outweigh the clearer exposition.
